introduction: On this fifth Sunday of Lent, Isaiah announces that God is doing something new, making a way in the desert. In the Gospel, a woman caught in adultery is brought to Jesus, and he says, Let the one without sin cast the first stone; then he tells her, Neither do I condemn you; go, and sin no more. Paul counts everything as loss compared to knowing Christ. Let us receive Christ's mercy and begin anew.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, the Lord has done great things for us. Let us bring him our prayers.
intentions: For the Church: that she may defend the dignity of every person, especially sinners and those who are condemned by others. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are publicly shamed or judged: that they may meet the mercy of Christ. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who are quick to condemn others: that they may first look into their own hearts. Let us pray to the Lord.
For prisoners and all who seek a new beginning: that God may make a way for them in the desert. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that, forgiven by Christ, we may go and sin no more. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: Lord God, you make all things new. Forgive our sins, free us from judging others, and help us to press on toward the prize of our calling in Christ. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: Neither do I condemn you
reflection.body:
Isaiah speaks to people who are always looking back at the past. God tells them: "Don't remember the former things... Behold, I will do a new thing. It springs out now. Don't you know it? I will even make a way in the wilderness, and rivers in the desert." God is not finished with us.

In the Gospel, the scribes and Pharisees bring a woman to Jesus, "a woman taken in adultery," and make her stand in front of everyone. They quote the law that she should be stoned and ask, "What then do you say about her?" It is a trap. They do not care about her; they want to accuse Jesus.

Jesus bends down and writes on the ground. When they keep pressing him, he straightens up and says, "He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her." Then he writes on the ground again. One by one they leave, "beginning from the oldest." Finally, Jesus is left alone with the woman.

He asks her, "Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?" She says, "No one, Lord." And Jesus says, "Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more." He does not pretend that sin does not matter. But he gives her what no one else would: mercy and a future.

Paul tells us how knowing Christ changes everything: "I count all things to be a loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus, my Lord." And he describes his attitude: "forgetting the things which are behind and stretching forward to the things which are before, I press on."

This week, notice when you are quick to pick up a stone against someone. Put it down. And bring your own sins to Jesus in confession. Hear him say to you: neither do I condemn you; go, and sin no more.
